title: Before the Promised Land Had a Leader, It Had a Servant: The Hidden Years Joshua Spent in the Shadows
paragraphs:
Before the Promised Land Had a Leader, It Had a Servant: The Hidden Years Joshua Spent in the Shadows
The man who conquered Jericho first learned how to disappear, and the years nobody applauded became the years God used to prepare a deliverer.
Most people want the moment Joshua stood before Israel.
Few want the years Joshua stood behind Moses.
We celebrate the walls of Jericho falling.
God celebrates the decades of obedience that happened before a single wall ever moved.
That is where many believers struggle today.
We want purpose without preparation.
Influence without obscurity.
Leadership without servanthood.
Yet when Scripture introduces Joshua, it does not first introduce a conqueror.
It introduces a servant.
The first time we are given a significant description of Joshua, Scripture says:
"But his servant Joshua son of Nun, a young man, did not depart from the tent." (Exodus 33:11)
The Hebrew text calls him יְהוֹשֻׁעַ (Yehoshua).
His name literally means:
"Yahweh is salvation."
Centuries later, this same name would be carried into Greek as:
Ἰησοῦς (Iēsous)
The very name used for Jesus.
This is not an accident.
Joshua was never meant to point people to himself.
He was meant to point forward to Christ.
Joshua would lead Israel into an earthly inheritance.
Jesus would lead sinners into an eternal one.
And before Joshua could become a picture of Christ's leadership, God first shaped him through years that nobody noticed.
That should encourage someone reading this today.
Because some of you feel forgotten.
You are serving faithfully.
Praying faithfully.
Giving faithfully.
Showing up faithfully.
And nothing seems to be changing.
You see others being promoted.
Others being recognized.
Others receiving opportunities.
Meanwhile, you remain in the shadows.
Joshua understands.
Because Joshua spent years in places where his name was barely mentioned.
Think about it.
When Moses climbed Mount Sinai, Joshua accompanied him partway up the mountain.
When Israel fought Amalek, Joshua fought while Moses prayed.
When the spies entered Canaan, Joshua was one of the few who remained faithful.
Again and again Joshua appears.
But never at the center.
Never demanding attention.
Never promoting himself.
Never building a platform.
Never trying to become Moses.
He simply remained faithful where God placed him.
Modern culture teaches people to make themselves known.
The Kingdom often teaches people to become unknown.
Jesus Himself said:
"Whoever would be great among you must be your servant." (Mark 10:43)
The Greek word used is:
διάκονος (diakonos)
A servant.
One who waits on others.
One who puts himself second.
One who serves without demanding recognition.
Joshua learned that long before he ever wore the mantle of leadership.
Many people think God prepares leaders by giving them authority.
Scripture repeatedly shows God prepares leaders by giving them opportunities to serve.
David learned among sheep.
Joseph learned in prison.
Moses learned in the wilderness.
Joshua learned beside another man's calling.
And perhaps that is one of the hardest lessons of all.
Serving faithfully when somebody else receives the spotlight.
Many people can handle obscurity.
Few can handle assisting someone else's success.
Yet Joshua did.
For years.
Decades.
Without bitterness.
Without rebellion.
Without entitlement.
Without demanding his turn.
Imagine watching Moses perform miracles.
Imagine seeing Moses speak with God.
Imagine hearing Israel praise Moses.
Imagine being constantly identified as "Moses' assistant."
Year after year.
Decade after decade.
Would you remain faithful?
Would you still serve?
Would you still trust God's timing?
Joshua did.
And because he did, God entrusted him with more.
The Bible says:
"Now therefore arise, go over this Jordan, you and all this people." (Joshua 1:2)
Suddenly the servant becomes the leader.
The assistant becomes the commander.
The shadow becomes the visible representative.
But what many people miss is that Joshua's promotion was not sudden.
It only looked sudden.
The public moment was built on private faithfulness.
What appeared overnight had actually been decades in the making.
That truth changes everything.
Because some of you are measuring God's work by what is visible.
God is measuring by what is invisible.
While you are worried about advancement, He is concerned with formation.
While you are asking when, He is shaping who.
While you are praying for the platform, He is preparing the person.
The greatest danger is not arriving late.
The greatest danger is arriving before God has finished preparing you.
Joshua was ready because Joshua had been refined.
The wilderness that frustrated Israel was also the classroom that trained Joshua.
The waiting that discouraged others developed him.
The delays that seemed pointless became preparation.
Nothing was wasted.
Not a single year.
Not a single disappointment.
Not a single hidden season.
That same principle appears throughout Scripture.
Romans 8:28 declares:
"And we know that for those who love God all things work together for good."
The Greek phrase πάντα συνεργεῖ εἰς ἀγαθόν (panta synergei eis agathon) means all things are being worked together toward God's good purpose.
Not some things.
All things.
Even the waiting.
Even the hidden years.
Even the seasons that seem forgotten.
Even the tears nobody saw.
Even the prayers that felt unanswered.
God was writing Joshua's story long before Joshua understood it.
And God may be writing yours in ways you cannot yet see.
Perhaps you feel overlooked.
Perhaps you feel invisible.
Perhaps you feel like everyone else is moving forward while you remain in the same place.
Do not mistake hiddenness for abandonment.
Joshua's greatest preparation happened where nobody was applauding.
Your hidden season may be holier than you realize.
Your ordinary faithfulness may be shaping extraordinary fruit.
Your service may be preparing a future assignment that only God can see.
The Gospel itself follows this pattern.
Jesus spent roughly thirty years in relative obscurity before three years of public ministry.
The Savior of the world spent more time preparing than preaching.
More time hidden than visible.
More time serving than leading.
Then came the cross.
The ultimate scandal.
The innocent Lamb was treated like a criminal.
The Author of life was nailed to a tree.
Yet what looked like history's greatest defeat became history's greatest victory.
That is the Gospel.
That is grace.
That is God's pattern.
He specializes in transforming hidden seasons into holy purposes.
He turns wildernesses into training grounds.
He turns failures into testimonies.
He turns crosses into empty tombs.
He turns scandal into grace.
And because of Jesus Christ, He can rewrite your story too.
Maybe you are still in your Joshua years.
Still serving.
Still waiting.
Still wondering.
Do not quit now.
God has never forgotten where He placed you.
The same God who saw Joshua in the shadows sees you.
The same God who called Joshua forward at the right time knows exactly when your season will change.
Until then, stay faithful.
Stay humble.
Stay teachable.
Stay close to Christ.
Because the years before leadership are often the years that determine whether leadership will glorify God when it arrives.
Sometimes one shared testimony becomes the reminder that another believer desperately needed.
A season of serving, waiting, learning, and trusting God behind the scenes? Your testimony may strengthen someone else's faith today.
Supporting Gospel Warrior is more than supporting a page—it is helping advance a ministry dedicated to pointing people to Jesus Christ.
Every share helps biblical truth reach someone who may be struggling, doubting, wandering, or searching for hope.
One day you may discover that the season you begged God to end was the very season He used to prepare you for everything He promised.
